05-speed-tilted.summary: Ship sqlite code, keep jsonl default for one release, migrate safely in off-hours, then opt in and later flip default after soak.

steps.action: Implement SqliteMemory in mirofish_lab/memory.py with sqlite3-only persistence, thread/process-safe writes, query helpers, and loud failures on write errors; keep LocalMemory signature unchanged as a compatibility shim that still reads legacy JSONL.
steps.rollback: Disable sqlite backend selection and route all persistence back to jsonl.
steps.observability: Unit tests for read/write parity, exceptions on failed writes, and legacy JSONL read compatibility.

steps.action: Add Agent backend selection in mirofish_lab/agent.py with backend="sqlite" support and MIROFISH_MEMORY_BACKEND default resolution, preserving jsonl as the default.
steps.rollback: Revert Agent backend selection to jsonl-only default behavior.
steps.observability: Constructor tests confirming default=jsonl, explicit sqlite opt-in, and no per-experiment changes required.

steps.action: Add migration helper migrate_jsonl_to_sqlite() that imports every .mirofish_memory/*.jsonl record into memory.db with batching suitable for low IOPS and reconciliation checks.
steps.rollback: Delete .mirofish_memory/memory.db and rerun import from JSONL.
steps.observability: Migration test results, imported row counts, duplicate detection, and reconciliation output.

steps.action: Add concurrency, restart-persistence, and migration validation tests covering simultaneous agents, sqlite_busy behavior, and recovery of prior JSONL history.
steps.rollback: Redeploy previous version and keep jsonl-only execution.
steps.observability: CI test suite results for concurrent writes, restart readback, and migration correctness.

steps.action: Create the SQLite schema and initial .mirofish_memory/memory.db in an off-hours window, then run a one-time import of existing JSONL data into SQLite without changing the default backend.
steps.rollback: Drop the newly created SQLite database and keep JSONL backend active.
steps.observability: Table/index creation success, import counts, sqlite_busy rate, and low-level IOPS during migration.

steps.action: Keep JSONL as the default backend for one release while exposing sqlite only via explicit opt-in and documenting the migration path and support escalation flow.
steps.rollback: Set MIROFISH_MEMORY_BACKEND=jsonl and keep sqlite opt-in only.
steps.observability: Opt-in usage, support tickets, documentation readiness, and customer announcement completion.

steps.action: Enable sqlite opt-in for users who set MIROFISH_MEMORY_BACKEND=sqlite after migration validation passes, while keeping legacy JSONL files readable.
steps.rollback: Switch MIROFISH_MEMORY_BACKEND back to jsonl and stop using memory.db.
steps.observability: Import validation status, sqlite write errors, history lookup correctness, and memory inspection behavior.

steps.action: Monitor sqlite opt-in traffic and keep JSONL files retained until 7 days pass with no JSONL reads after cutover; if busy errors rise, pause sqlite writes and fall back to JSONL.
steps.rollback: Re-enable JSONL writes and pause SQLite writes until contention clears.
steps.observability: sqlite_busy_errors, JSONL read count, write latency, and fallback frequency.

steps.action: After one full release notice period and 24h of low sqlite write errors, flip the default backend to sqlite for new runs, keeping an immediate env-var rollback to jsonl.
steps.rollback: Revert default backend to jsonl without redeploying code.
steps.observability: sqlite_write_error_rate, incident status, Friday/launch-window constraints, and default-selection metrics.

steps.action: After 7 days with no JSONL reads following cutover, remove legacy JSONL files or archive them per policy, leaving the single SQLite table as the inspectable store.
steps.rollback: Restore JSONL files from backup and switch backend back to jsonl.
steps.observability: JSONL read telemetry, backup integrity, final table presence, and user-accessibility checks.
